docs.title: Markdown Features Starter
docs.text:
A small docs site built from plain .md files. Every page demonstrates GUI features that plain Markdown on GitHub cannot do, such as tabs, callouts, copy buttons, diagrams, and a search box.

Get started See the features

docs.title: What is inside
docs.text:
• Copy buttons

    Every code block gets a copy icon automatically. Try it on Getting Started.

  • Tabs and switchers

    Switch between Windows, macOS and Linux instructions in one click.

  • Callouts and collapsibles

    Notes, warnings, tips and expandable sections. See Callouts.

  • Diagrams and math

    Mermaid flowcharts, Gantt charts and LaTeX equations. See Diagrams and Math.

  • Code block extras

    Line numbers, highlighted lines, titles, diffs and annotations. See Code Blocks.

  • Interactive bits

    Custom buttons, copy-to-clipboard for any text, and more. See Interactive Bits.

docs.title: Built-in features you get for free
docs.text:
• Full-text search (top right)
  • Light and dark mode toggle (top right)
  • Sidebar and table of contents built from your headings
  • Hover anchor links on every heading
  • Mobile-friendly layout
  • Your own content (that is the next step)

Where to go next

Open any .md file in the docs/ folder, change some text, and save. If mkdocs serve is running, the page refreshes by itself.

Make it yours

Use the round button at the bottom right (or press Alt+T) to switch themes, change colors, zoom, font and page width. See Theme Lab for details.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
Pick your operating system. Your choice is remembered across every tab group on the site.

WindowsmacOSLinux 
py -m pip install -r requirements.txt

python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt

python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt

Note

Python 3.8 or newer is required. Check with python --version.

docs.title: 2. Run the site locally
docs.text:
mkdocs serve

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in your browser.

docs.title: 3. Build the final website
docs.text:
mkdocs build

This creates a site/ folder of plain HTML files that you can upload to any web host.

docs.title: 4. Publish for free (GitHub Pages)
docs.text: mkdocs gh-deploy

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
md-docs-starter/
├── mkdocs.yml          # site settings, menu, theme, extensions
├── requirements.txt    # what to install
└── docs/
    ├── index.md        # home page
    ├── getting-started.md
    ├── features/       # one page per feature group
    └── javascripts/    # custom scripts (math rendering)

docs.title: What each setting does
docs.text:
Open mkdocs.yml and look at these blocks.

mkdocs.yml
theme:
  name: material
  features:                      # (1)!
    - content.code.copy          # (2)!
    - navigation.tabs
  1. The features list turns individual interface features on or off.
  2. This single line is what adds the copy button to every code block.

docs.title: Add a new page
docs.text:
1. Create a file such as docs/my-page.md.

  2. Add it to the nav: section in mkdocs.yml:

    nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - My Page: my-page.md

  3. Save. The page appears in the menu.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
Pages that carry tags in their front matter are listed here automatically.

To tag a page, add this at the very top of its .md file:

---
tags:
  - my-tag
  - another-tag
---

docs.title: Theme Lab
docs.text:
This page explains every display control. All of them live in one place: the round settings button in the bottom-right corner of every page (or press Alt+T).

Your choices are remembered

Settings are stored in your browser, so they stay the same on every page and on your next visit.

docs.title: Light and dark mode
docs.text: Use the Mode buttons in the settings panel (or press Alt+D). The Midnight and Graphite presets switch to dark mode and pick matching colors. The page keeps a fixed palette, so there is no flash of the wrong theme when a page loads.

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text: Keys Action Alt+T Open or close settings Alt+= Zoom in Alt+- Zoom out Alt+0 Reset zoom Alt+W Toggle fit screen / centered Alt+D Toggle light / dark mode / or S Focus the search box Esc Close the settings panel

docs.title: Click-to-zoom images
docs.text: Every image on the site opens in a zoomable lightbox when clicked. Try it:

docs.title: Change the defaults for everyone
docs.text:
Open docs/javascripts/ui.js and edit the block at the top:

docs/javascripts/ui.js
var DEFAULTS = {
  preset: "Indigo",
  primary: "indigo",
  accent: "indigo",
  fit: true,       // true = full screen width
  zoom: 1.1,       // 1.1 = 10% larger on first launch
  font: "default",
  density: "comfortable",
  progress: true
};

Visitors who already saved their own settings keep them. Anyone opening the site for the first time gets the new defaults.

docs.title: Change the layout with CSS only
docs.text:
If you prefer CSS, edit docs/stylesheets/extra.css. For example, to limit the page width on huge monitors:

docs/stylesheets/extra.css
html.fit-width .md-grid {
  max-width: 2000px;   /* instead of "none" */
}

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Pick a topic. Each page demonstrates one group of features you can use in your own .md files.

  • Callouts and Collapsibles

    Notes, warnings, tips and expandable sections.

  • Code Blocks

    Copy buttons, line numbers, highlights, tabs and diffs.

  • Diagrams and Math

    Mermaid diagrams and LaTeX equations.

  • Text, Layout and Media

    Styling, tables, images, buttons and icons.

  • Interactive Bits

    Custom buttons, converters and small tools.

  • UI Showcase

    Stat cards, progress bars, badges and a timeline.

docs.title: Callouts (admonitions)
docs.text:
Note

A note. Use it for neutral extra information.

Summary

A short summary of the page.

Info

Useful background information.

Tip

A helpful shortcut or best practice.

Success

Something completed or worked.

Question

A question or FAQ prompt.

Warning

Be careful with this step.

Failure

Something that failed or an error case.

Danger

A serious risk, such as data loss.

Bug

A known bug or issue.

Example

A worked example.

Quote

A quotation or reference text.

docs.title: Side-by-side callout
docs.text:
Side note

This box floats to the right of the text next to it.

Text placed after an inline end callout wraps around it. This is handy for short asides, definitions and quick references, so the main paragraph stays uncluttered. Keep adding text here to see it flow beside the box, and keep going until the paragraph is a little longer than the box itself.

docs.title: FAQ-style accordion
docs.text:
How do I add a new page?

Create a .md file in docs/ and list it under nav: in mkdocs.yml.

Can I change the colors?

Yes. Edit the palette block in mkdocs.yml.

Does it work on mobile?

Yes. The layout adapts to small screens automatically.

docs.title: Math (LaTeX)
docs.text:
Inline math: \(E = mc^2\) and \(a^2 + b^2 = c^2\).

Display math:

\[ \int_0^\infty e^{-x^2}\,dx = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2} \]

A matrix:

\[ A = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \det A = ad - bc \]

Aligned equations:

\[ \begin{aligned} (a+b)^2 &= a^2 + 2ab + b^2 \\ (a-b)^2 &= a^2 - 2ab + b^2 \end{aligned} \]

Greek letters and sums: \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \sum_{i=1}^{n} i = \frac{n(n+1)}{2}\)

docs.title: 01 Confirmation
docs.text:
What the event is "Fast-Track Physical AI: Build, Simulate and Deploy With NVIDIA's Open Stack" is a hands-on workshop about physical AI, meaning AI that controls robots and machines in the real world. You'll likely learn to build robot behaviors, test them in simulation (NVIDIA's Isaac Sim and Omniverse tools), and then deploy them.

When and where - Date and time: October 7 (tomorrow), 9:00 a.m. IST - Venue: WeWork EON Free Zone, Kharadi, Cluster D, Wing 4, Pune - Arrival: The email asks you to arrive 30 minutes early, so by about 8:30 a.m.

What you need to do before the workshop 1. Review the agenda and prerequisites. There's a link in the email (it says "here"). The prerequisites are mandatory, so check what software or knowledge you're expected to have. 2. Create an NVIDIA Developer Program account. It's free and gives you access to the labs and training before and after the event. 3. Make sure your internet is good. The labs likely run in the cloud, so you need about 5 Mbps download and 1-2 Mbps upload.

What to bring - Your laptop (required) - A valid government ID for check-in (required) - Optional: your own project files, such as CAD models (STEP, OBJ, FBX, JT), USD assets, ROS bags, sample videos, or robot logs, if you want to try them during the session

One thing to note: "First-come, first-served" refers to seating, so arriving early helps you get a good spot.
